notes.text: The 4-state busy beaver champion (Brady, 1983). Started on a BLANK tape it scribbles back and forth for exactly 107 steps, prints 13 ones, and halts. No 4-state machine that halts does more — proving that took years.
Leave the input EMPTY (ε) and press run. The head wanders left of its starting cell — that's why this lives on the two-way infinite tape.
The 5-state version was only settled in 2024: it runs 47,176,870 steps before halting. Six states already outruns the observable universe. This is where computation stops being predictable.

meta.title: The 4-state busy beaver
meta.blurb: The most famous tiny machine in computer science: from a blank tape it runs exactly 107 steps, prints 13 ones, and halts — the maximum any 4-state machine can do. Run it with empty input.
